originalRequirement: Verify the 2026–2027 international study requirement, elective level and overlap conditions, and entry requirements for qualitative research, the public-issues capstone and the thesis.
essentialEvidence: Verify the progression rules that apply to September 2026 entrants for entry to qualitative research (USG2020) and the graduation project and thesis (USG3220). Confirm the precise treatment of any overlapping profiling courses under the applicable regulations.
officialAlternative: The current profiling and exchange pages resolve the advanced-level and international study requirements. The 2026–2027 CursusPlanner verifies course-specific capstone prerequisites and confirms the qualitative research and graduation units, but points to the OER for their progression rules. The public regulation index and available thesis handbook offer only earlier editions. The same essential progression evidence is still incomplete.

At least 15 EC at level 3 out of 37.5 EC in profiling, and at least 15 EC in an international context for entrants from 2020 onward. The latter may be earned through English-taught study or study at a foreign institution.

The 2026–2027 exchange briefing, prepared in 2025 for students applying by December 2025, calls for 15 EC at advanced level and identifies 7.5 international EC in its profiling section, plus non-duplication with the B&O major. This narrower scope is consistent with the 7.5 EC required English-taught major course. It is not a replacement for the 15 EC programme-wide rule. Its overlap guidance concerns exchange; the current general overlap clause was not located.
The required Comparative Analysis of Political Institutions is taught in English and includes a paper in English.
The programme credit table independently verifies the 180 EC allocation and places methods courses before qualitative research and the graduation phase.
Confirms preparation in period three, independent research, written thesis and presentation in period four. It does not provide the entry threshold.
Provides the previous year’s research, supervision and assessment details. It does not establish the 2026–2027 entry conditions.
Lists only the 2025–2026 and earlier OERs publicly. Targeted search for the 2026–2027 progression rules did not locate a current OER.

The earlier regulation required USG1030 and USG1050 before USG2020 and USG2020 before thesis entry. The previous Annex 1 differs from the present first-year list. These exact course conditions cannot be transferred without current confirmation.

result: Second official-source attempt. Verified profiling and capstone rules. Progression evidence remains incomplete.
